h1: DTF Printing or Embroidery: Which to Choose?
estratto: Elegant, long-lasting embroidery or colourful, versatile DTF printing? Here's how to choose the right technique for your custom clothing.

paragrafi: Embroidery or DTF printing? The right way to personalise clothing depends on the fabric, the design and the effect you're after. Embroidery is all about elegance and durability, while DTF printing delivers vivid colours and versatility. Let's look at the real differences so you can see which one suits you.

sezioni.heading: DTF printing: colours and detail without limits
paragrafi: DTF (Direct to Film) printing transfers the design from a film onto the garment using the heat of a press. It's the ideal technique for complex graphics, photos, gradients and multicolour logos, with faithful, brilliant results.

It bonds to almost any fabric (cotton, blends, polyester and technical materials), stays light to the touch and is cost-effective even for a single piece. The downside: it stays flat, with no raised effect, and with very harsh or high-temperature washes it tends to wear out sooner than embroidery.
lista: You want vivid colours, gradients or detailed logos.
You're personalising t-shirts, hoodies or promotional clothing.
You're looking for a versatile, budget-friendly solution on a range of fabrics.
You prefer a light print, with no added thickness.

sezioni.heading: Embroidery: elegance and lasting resistance
paragrafi: Embroidery weaves the threads directly into the fabric, creating logos and lettering with a three-dimensional effect. It conveys a premium image and is the classic choice for company uniforms, hotels, restaurants and quality garments.

It's the most durable technique: it doesn't fade and withstands hundreds of washes while keeping an impeccable look. Less suited to highly detailed or gradient graphics and to light, stretchy fabrics, it becomes more expensive on large logos.
lista: You want an elegant, refined and professional look.
You're personalising polo shirts, hoodies, jackets, caps or uniforms.
You need a logo that lasts over time and stands up to frequent washing.
You have a simple design, with no tiny details or gradients.

sezioni.heading: DTF or embroidery: the comparison at a glance
paragrafi: In short, the two techniques answer different needs:
lista: Design: DTF for complex, colourful graphics, embroidery for simple logos and lettering.
Fabrics: DTF on practically anything, embroidery ideal on thick, structured garments.
Durability: embroidery holds up better to frequent washing and high temperatures.
Effect: DTF flat and light, embroidery raised with a premium look.
Cost: DTF cost-effective even for a few pieces and large graphics, embroidery excellent on small logos.

faq.domanda: Which lasts longer, embroidery or DTF printing?
faq.risposta: Embroidery is more durable and withstands hundreds of washes without deteriorating. Quality DTF printing generally lasts 50-100 washes, great for most uses but more sensitive to very hot, aggressive washing.

faq.domanda: How much does embroidery cost compared to DTF printing?
faq.risposta: Embroidery costs more, especially on large logos or intricate designs, because the price grows with the size and the number of stitches. DTF printing is cheaper and is worthwhile even for large, colourful graphics. For an accurate quote, all we need is to see your logo.

faq.domanda: Can DTF printing be done on any fabric?
faq.risposta: Yes, DTF bonds to almost any fabric: cotton, blends, polyester and technical materials. On very thick or structured garments, such as heavy hoodies and jackets, embroidery is often still the best choice.

faq.domanda: Embroidery or DTF printing for workwear?
faq.risposta: It depends on the garment and the image you want to project. Embroidery is perfect for polo shirts, jackets and representative uniforms with a simple logo. DTF is worthwhile for t-shirts and garments with colourful or detailed graphics. Often both techniques are used together.

faq.domanda: Is a minimum order required to personalise garments?
faq.risposta: No, we personalise even a single piece. With DTF printing you don't need large quantities to get a good price, while embroidery is cost-effective even on small logos and short runs.
